quote:
Prove the forge pipeline end to end with a real skinned character mesh instead of the cube placeholder, and fix whatever breaks along the way.

Take a real multi-material mesh with skin weights (the extracted hero body DMX you already import as the source, or a real custom character mesh if one is available in the environment — do not synthesize a stand-in cube) and run it through the whole active pipeline: import, fit, retarget weights/names onto the hero skeleton, assign hero materials, export the replacement DMX, stage it against the byte-identical S2V-extracted vmdl, and compile with CSDK13's resourcecompiler on the real content path. The extracted vmdl and its DMX/materials remain the source of truth — the addon only owns the replacement mesh, retargeting, and materials. Do not add any KV3 parsing, vmdl writing, or hero-vmdl reconstruction; the existing gate/selftest must still reject that, and if a real blocker forces a code change, keep it inside the mesh/retarget/material/stage/compile path.

Debug and repair every failure that appears on the way to a successful compile with the real mesh. Then verify and report the concrete numbers: source mesh vs exported DMX vertex and bone counts, number of material assignments carried through, the staged vmdl SHA-256 staying identical to the extraction hash, resourcecompiler return code plus compiled/failed counts and warnings, and the resulting .vmdl_c path and size. Also run the unit tests, the gate, and the selftest.

Done when: A real skinned, multi-material mesh goes through import → fit → retarget → material assignment → DMX export → unchanged extracted-vmdl staging → CSDK13 compile, and: the exported DMX's vertex count and bone count match the source mesh and its weights survive (not a cube or placeholder), the staged vmdl SHA-256 is byte-identical to the S2V extraction, resourcecompiler returns 0 and produces the .vmdl_c (path and size reported), unit tests, gate, and the anti-KV3 selftest all pass, and the source tree still contains no KV3 parser or vmdl writer.

Own this outcome end to end: inspect, implement, run, read failures, repair, and verify within this turn. Do not stop to report an intermediate step. Stop for a user-only decision or approval instead of guessing. Finish with what you changed, how you verified it, and what is still open.
